snapshot.title: UPSC History: August Offer & Cripps Mission
snapshot.exam_hook: 🏔️ UPSC History Hook: 1940: August Offer. Vinoba: 1st Satyagrahi. 1942: Cripps Mission (Failed). Post-dated check: Gandhi. Secede right: Cripps.

quick_notes.title: August Offer (1940)
quick_notes.detail: By Linlithgow. Promised "Dominion Status" after the war and an advisory war council. Rejected by INC because it didn't offer independence and by League because it didn't offer Pakistan.
quick_notes.explanation: The August Offer was a proposal made in August 1940 by Lord Linlithgow, who was the British Viceroy (the highest British official) in India. It promised that after World War Two ended, India would get Dominion Status, which means it would become a self-governing country within the British Empire, like Canada or Australia, still keeping the British monarch as head of state. The offer also suggested creating an advisory war council where Indian leaders could give suggestions but not make decisions about the war. The Indian National Congress (INC) rejected the offer because it did not give full independence. The All India Muslim League rejected it because the offer did not promise to create

quick_notes.title: Individual Satyagraha (1940)
quick_notes.detail: Launched to assert the right to free speech against the war. 1st Satyagrahi: Vinoba Bhave. 2nd: Jawaharlal Nehru. It was "limited" to avoid hindering the war effort while protesting.
quick_notes.explanation: Individual Satyagraha (1940) was a protest movement launched by the Indian National Congress, which is the main political party that led India's freedom struggle. The purpose was to assert the right to free speech, meaning the freedom to speak and write openly, which the British government had banned during World War II, a global war that started in 1939. The first person to offer this protest, called the first Satyagrahi, was Vinoba Bhave, a close follower of Mahatma Gandhi. The second Satyagrahi was Jawaharlal Nehru, who later became India's first Prime Minister. This protest was called "limited" because it was designed to avoid hindering, or slowing down, the British war effort against the enemy, while still allowing Indians to peacefully protest the war.

quick_notes.title: Cripps Mission (1942)
quick_notes.detail: Led by Stafford Cripps. Promised "Dominion Status" and a "Constituent Assembly" where provinces could OPT OUT (seed of partition). Gandhi called it a "Post-dated check".
quick_notes.explanation: The Cripps Mission was a British effort during World War II, led by Sir Stafford Cripps, to gain Indian cooperation for the war. It promised India "Dominion Status," which means full self-government while still being part of the British Empire, like Canada or Australia. The mission also offered to create a "Constituent Assembly," a group of elected Indians who would write India's own constitution after the war. However, the proposal allowed any province to "OPT OUT," meaning it could choose not to join the new India and possibly form a separate country—this clause planted the seed for the later partition into India and Pakistan. Mahatma Gandhi called the offer a "post-dated check," meaning it promised something valuable in the future but gave nothing real immediately. Because the British did not commit to immediate independence and kept wartime control, Indian leaders rejected the proposal.

quick_notes.title: Failure of Cripps
quick_notes.detail: INC rejected it due to Dominion Status and the "Option to secede". League rejected it because it didn't explicitly grant Pakistan.
quick_notes.explanation: The Cripps Mission was a British effort in 1942 to gain Indian support for World War Two by offering a future plan for self-rule. The Indian National Congress (INC), the main political party, rejected the offer because it only promised Dominion Status, meaning India would remain a self-governing part of the British Empire with the British monarch as head of state, rather than full independence. The INC also objected to the "Option to secede," which would have allowed any province to leave the future Indian union, weakening a unified India. The All India Muslim League, a party representing many Muslims, rejected the plan because it did not explicitly promise a separate nation called Pakistan. As a result, both major Indian political groups refused the Cripps proposals, and the mission failed.

quick_notes.title: Impact of Failure
quick_notes.detail: Led to massive frustration and the realization that the British would not leave voluntarily. Set the stage for "Quit India".
quick_notes.explanation: The failure of the Cripps Mission in 1942 caused huge anger and disappointment among Indian leaders, because they understood that the British government was not willing to give India independence or even full control of its own affairs after World War Two. This mission, led by a British politician named Sir Stafford Cripps, offered India a plan for a new constitution but gave the British full power over defense and allowed any province to stay separate, which the Indian National Congress (INC) rejected. This realization that Britain would not leave peacefully or voluntarily led directly to the launching of the "Quit India" movement in August 1942, where the INC demanded an immediate end to British rule. In short, the breakdown of talks convinced Indian leaders that only a mass struggle, not negotiations, would force the British to leave India.

topic_title: UPSC History: August Offer & Cripps Mission
lesson_intro: Today we study the 'WWII Diplomacy'. With the British facing defeat in Europe, they tried to win over Indian support through a series of offers. We study the August Offer (1940), the start of 'Individual Satyagraha' by Vinoba Bhave, and the failed Cripps Mission (1942). For UPSC, focus on why Gandhi called the Cripps offer a 'Post-dated check on a crashing bank'. This is the final diplomatic prelude to the great Quit India struggle.
